chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Basir, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike that I rent a single millstone, and then rent it out for more than what I rented it for, unless an incident occurs in it or a debt is incurred in it.'

key_terms.أُؤَاجِرُهَا: I rent it out (as a lessor)
key_terms.حَدَثًا: Incident or occurrence (implying damage or change in condition)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on subletting rented equipment like a millstone?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prohibits subletting a single millstone at a higher price to avoid *rib al-nasi'ah* (profit from rent), distinguishing it from legitimate profit derived from actual usage or value addition. This ruling, found in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, establishes a key principle in Shia commercial jurisprudence regarding the permissibility of *ujrah* (rent) contracts, allowing exceptions only for tangible changes like damage or incurred debts, thereby preventing speculative exploitation of fixed assets.
